h: Beaches, Slate and Mountains Close By
p: One of the joys of the Caernarfon area is how quickly you can swap one kind of day out for another. Gypsy Wood Park offers a slower, gentler pace, but within a short drive you'll find sandy beaches, mountain railways and fascinating industrial heritage.

Dinas Dinlle, a long sandy beach south-west of Caernarfon, is a great spot for a paddle and sandcastles, with views over to Anglesey and the Llŷn Peninsula. Inigo Jones Slateworks at Groeslon offers a chance to see slate being worked and even try your hand at engraving, which kids find surprisingly fun.

Over in Llanberis, the National Slate Museum is free to visit and tells the story of the quarrymen who shaped this part of Wales. The Snowdon Mountain Railway also sets off from Llanberis, climbing towards the summit of Yr Wyddfa when the weather and season allow. Greenwood Family Park, near Y Felinheli, is another popular outdoor attraction if you're after more adventure play.

For a visit to Gypsy Wood Park itself, take your time. Let the kids explore the trails and play areas at their own speed, and pack a picnic to enjoy among the trees. With so much of it outdoors, waterproofs and sturdy shoes are your best friends. If the weather looks settled, it's well worth combining a morning in the woods with an afternoon on the sand at Dinas Dinlle, giving the kids the best of both worlds in a single day.
